metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (VB6 form file frmCustomer.frm) with a deployable entry point (Form_Load() subroutine) and direct database connection configuration present. Single deployable desktop EXE.
metadata.archetype_justification: Application performs database writes (INSERT INTO Customers) with user-specific data (CreatedBy via Environ(USERNAME)). Owns persistent state in the Access .mdb database. CRUD operations on business entities (Customers).

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.10 yields Not Ready band but 11 High findings (below >=12 threshold) force Remediation Required tier. 5 questions are Not Evaluated (surface-gated: INF-Q9, SEC-Q1, OPS-Q5, OPS-Q7, OPS-Q9) which reduces the High count below the >=12 Not Ready threshold.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: Application is extremely small (~40 lines of logic), written in an unsupported language (VB6) that cannot be containerized or deployed to the cloud. No identifiable modules to extract incrementally. Strangler Fig not applicable. Full rewrite carries low risk due to minimal scope.

findings.title: Managed Compute — Win32 desktop EXE with no cloud compute
findings.description: All compute is a Win32 desktop EXE (VB6 runtime) running locally on individual Windows laptops. No cloud compute, no managed container orchestration, no serverless functions.
findings.gap: No managed compute of any kind. Zero cloud presence — runs entirely on end-user devices with no central management, no elasticity, and no operational visibility.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the application as a cloud-native web service and deploy on managed compute (ECS/Fargate or Lambda).

findings.title: Managed Databases — Self-managed Access database on file share
findings.description: Database is a self-managed Microsoft Access 2003 .mdb file on a Windows SMB file share. SQL Server 2012 reporting database also self-managed. No managed database services.
findings.gap: All databases self-managed on network file shares (Access) and on-premises SQL Server. No automated failover, no managed backups, no scaling.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon Aurora or RDS PostgreSQL. Use AWS DMS for data migration and AWS SCT for schema conversion.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration — No orchestration, hardcoded batch sync
findings.description: No workflow orchestration. Nightly DTS/SSIS sync is a hardcoded scheduled job with no managed orchestration, no error handling, and no visibility.
findings.gap: Unmanaged DTS/SSIS workflow with no retry logic, no error notification, and no state management.
findings.recommendation: Implement AWS Step Functions for multi-step business operations in the cloud rebuild.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming — No messaging infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. All operations synchronous. No mechanism to notify other systems of changes. Only integration is nightly batch DTS/SSIS sync.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries. Customer record changes invisible to other systems until nightly batch.
findings.recommendation: Implement EventBridge or SNS for customer state-change events in the cloud rebuild.

findings.title: Network Security — No network segmentation or isolation
findings.description: No VPC, no private subnets, no security groups. Application connects directly from laptops to SMB file share. Database accessible to any machine on the network.
findings.gap: No network security controls. Database directly accessible on file share with hardcoded password. No segmentation between user devices and data store.
findings.recommendation: Deploy replacement service in VPC with private subnets, least-privilege security groups, and VPC endpoints.

findings.title: API Entry Point — No gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API gateway, no load balancer, no CloudFront. Desktop EXE connects directly to file-based database with no HTTP entry point.
findings.gap: No managed entry point. Direct database access from end-user devices with no intermediary.
findings.recommendation: Deploy replacement service behind API Gateway with throttling, authentication, and request validation.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — No dynamic capacity management
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Desktop EXE on laptops with single .mdb file on single file server. Cannot scale up or down.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling. System cannot handle concurrent access — README notes 'record locked' errors.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling on compute and data layers when deploying to AWS.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery — No automated backups
findings.description: No automated backup configuration. Access .mdb on single file server with no backup strategy, no PITR, no cross-region replication. Database corrupts monthly with no documented recovery.
findings.gap: No backup infrastructure. Monthly corruption events combined with no automated backups create significant data loss risk.
findings.recommendation: Enable automated backups with PITR when migrating to RDS/Aurora. Test restore procedures regularly.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage — Zero IaC
findings.description: Zero infrastructure as code. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any IaC. All infrastructure manually provisioned.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. All infrastructure manually created. No reproducibility, no version control of infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in AWS CDK or Terraform before deploying the replacement service.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — No pipeline, manual compilation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodeBuild. Compiled on one developer's machine. Deployment is manual file copy.
findings.gap: No automated build, test, or deployment. Entire delivery depends on single developer manually compiling and distributing.
findings.recommendation: Establish CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline + CodeBuild) with automated build, test, security scanning, and deployment.

findings.title: Programming Languages — VB6 with no cloud-native tooling
findings.description: Application written in Visual Basic 6.0 (created 2005, last touched 2018). VB6 has no AWS SDK, no cloud-native tooling, unsupported runtime. Cannot run on Linux, containers, or Lambda.
findings.gap: VB6 is a language with no AWS SDK and no cloud-native tooling (same tier as COBOL and PowerBuilder). Cannot be modernized in place — requires full rewrite.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in a modern cloud-native language: Python 3.12+, TypeScript/Node.js 20+, or Java 21/Kotlin with Spring Boot 3.x.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices — Tightly-coupled single-form monolith
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith with no module boundaries. Single VB6 form file containing UI, business logic, data access, and configuration in one undifferentiated unit.
findings.gap: No module boundaries, no separation of concerns. Cannot be decomposed incrementally — no modules to extract.
findings.recommendation: Full rewrite with proper architecture. See Decomposition Strategy section.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication — 100% synchronous, no async patterns
findings.description: All operations synchronous. Blocking ADODB.Connection.Execute on UI thread. No message queues, no event emission, no callback patterns. For stateful-crud, async expected for cross-service state propagation.
findings.gap: 100% synchronous communication. State changes not propagated in real-time. Only integration is nightly batch sync.
findings.recommendation: Implement async patterns for state-change propagation (EventBridge events on customer create/update) in cloud rebuild.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling — All operations synchronous regardless of duration
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. Nightly DTS/SSIS sync is long-running with no status tracking, no callbacks, no visibility. UI thread blocks during database operations.
findings.gap: No async job processing for long-running operations. No status polling, no callbacks, no job queues.
findings.recommendation: Implement async job processing (SQS + Lambda workers or Step Functions) for operations exceeding 30 seconds.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy — No API, no versioning
findings.description: No API versioning strategy. Desktop app with no HTTP endpoints. Schema changes require simultaneous update of all deployed EXEs.
findings.gap: No versioning. Schema changes require lock-step deployment across all laptops.
findings.recommendation: Implement API versioning (URL path /v1/) from day one in the replacement web service.

findings.title: Service Discovery — Hardcoded database path
findings.description: All service endpoints hardcoded. Database path is a constant (S:\CRM\sales.mdb). No service registry, no dynamic discovery, no environment-based configuration.
findings.gap: Hardcoded infrastructure dependency. Cannot deploy to different environment without recompiling.
findings.recommendation: Use environment variables or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for service endpoints in the cloud rebuild.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — Data on legacy file system
findings.description: All data stored in Microsoft Access .mdb file on Windows SMB file share. No managed object storage, no parsing capabilities, no accessibility for modern workloads.
findings.gap: Data on legacy file system in proprietary format (Access .mdb). Not accessible for analytics, AI, or modern reporting.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to S3 for unstructured/document storage and managed database (Aurora/RDS) for structured data.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer — Raw SQL in UI code
findings.description: No data access layer. Raw ADODB connection and string-concatenated SQL directly in UI form code. SQL injection vulnerability. No parameterization, no repository pattern, no ORM.
findings.gap: Database access code directly in UI layer with no separation. SQL injection due to string concatenation.
findings.recommendation: Implement proper data access layer (repository pattern or ORM) with parameterized queries in cloud rebuild.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL — All engines past end-of-life
findings.description: Microsoft Access 2003 with Jet OLEDB 4.0 (discontinued, no patches since 2010). SQL Server 2012 (end of extended support July 2022). Both past EOL with no version pinning.
findings.gap: All database engines past EOL. No security patches available. Known vulnerabilities unpatched.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL. Pin explicit engine versions in IaC.

findings.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity — Minimal proprietary SQL
findings.description: No stored procedures, triggers, or complex proprietary SQL. Single INSERT statement with basic columns. Minor proprietary dependency: Now() function (Jet-specific) and Jet OLEDB 4.0 provider coupling.
findings.gap: Minor proprietary SQL dependency: Now() function and Jet OLEDB provider. No stored procedures but database engine coupling exists.
findings.recommendation: Replace Now() with CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and update connection driver when migrating. Lack of stored procedures makes migration straightforward.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest — No encryption, plaintext data on file share
findings.description: No encryption at rest. Access .mdb uses database-level password (not encryption). Data stored in plaintext on SMB share. Jet Database Password is trivially bypassed.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest. Customer data in plaintext on network file share. No KMS, no disk-level encryption.
findings.recommendation: Enable KMS encryption at rest on all data stores when migrating to AWS managed databases.

findings.title: API Authentication — No authentication mechanism
findings.description: No API authentication. Desktop app connects to database using single hardcoded shared password. No per-request auth, no OAuth2/JWT, no token-based auth.
findings.gap: No per-request authentication. All access uses single shared credential hardcoded in source.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT via Amazon Cognito with API Gateway authorizers in the replacement service.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration — No IdP integration
findings.description: No centralized identity provider integration. Application uses Environ(USERNAME) for attribution only — not authentication. No OIDC, no SAML, no SSO.
findings.gap: No centralized IdP. Application trusts Windows environment variable without verification.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or corporate IdP (Okta, Azure AD) via OIDC/SAML.

findings.title: Secrets Management — Plaintext credentials in source code
findings.description: Plaintext database password hardcoded in source code: Private Const DB_PW As String = 'crm2005pw'. Committed to git version control. Visible to anyone with repo access.
findings.gap: Critical: plaintext credentials in source code. No secrets management system. Password in git history since 2005.
findings.recommendation: Immediate: rotate password and remove from source. Use AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation for all credentials.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching — No patching strategy
findings.description: No patching strategy, no vulnerability scanning, no hardened images. VB6 runtime unsupported and unpatched. No SSM, no Inspector, no Snyk.
findings.gap: No patching or vulnerability management. VB6 runtime and Jet OLEDB are unpatched legacy components with known vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Use managed compute (Fargate/Lambda) to eliminate OS patching. Enable Amazon Inspector for vulnerability scanning.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — No security scanning
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No CI/CD pipeline to embed scanning into. Known SQL injection vulnerability unfixed since 2005.
findings.gap: Zero security scanning. No SAST, no DAST, no dependency scanning. SQL injection persists because no security tooling exists.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST (SonarQube/Semgrep), dependency scanning, and container scanning into CI/CD pipeline from day one.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — No instrumentation
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray. Errors silently swallowed with On Error Resume Next. No logging or telemetry.
findings.gap: Zero observability instrumentation. Operations fail silently. Cannot diagnose production issues.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry SDK and X-Ray from the start in the cloud rebuild.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — No SLOs or monitoring
findings.description: No SLO definitions. No monitoring. Only indication of system health is users verbally reporting record-locked errors.
findings.gap: No SLOs defined, no monitoring to support SLO tracking.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for critical user journeys when deploying replacement service. Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics — No metrics published
findings.description: No custom metrics. No business outcome tracking. Basic attribution (CreatedBy/CreatedOn) in database but no metric emission.
findings.gap: No business metrics. No visibility into usage, feature adoption, or business outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics for business events in the cloud rebuild.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting — No alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No anomaly detection. Database corruption and connection failures discovered by users, not by monitoring.
findings.gap: No alerting. Monthly corruption events discovered reactively.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms on error rates and latency. Add anomaly detection. Integrate with PagerDuty.

findings.title: Integration Testing — No automated tests
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. No unit tests, no integration tests. README states 'No tests.' SQL injection persists unfixed since 2005.
findings.gap: Zero test coverage. No quality gate. Changes validated only by manual testing on developer's machine.
findings.recommendation: Establish integration tests from day one in the replacement service. Run in CI pipeline.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — No ownership structure
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms, no CODEOWNERS, no team attribution. Monitoring is entirely reactive.
findings.gap: No observability ownership structure. Service health unmonitored and unowned.
findings.recommendation: Establish per-service dashboards with named owners when deploying replacement service.
